settingsAgentsNote: Disabled agents are left out of new sessions, task dispatch, new workspaces and the phone, and the daemon won't start them; ones already running keep going, and typing their command in a terminal still works. Only agents installed on this Mac are listed.

@settingsAgentsTitle.description: Title of the card of agent switches.

settingsAwakeNote: While Posse runs, the Mac doesn't sleep but the display still turns off; the coffee cup in the status bar toggles this too. “Keep Display On” keeps the display awake as well: when the display turns off, the screen locks with it.

@settingsAwakeNote.description: Note of the Prevent Sleep card; quotes the third segment's label.

@settingsAwakeTitle.description: Title of the card, and the label of its segmented control.

settingsDaemonNeedsRestart: The daemon is older than the window and can't be updated without disconnecting terminals; restart it once. Restarting closes all terminals.

@settingsDaemonNotConnected.description: About card: the daemon isn't reachable.

@settingsDaemonOldVersion.description: About card: a daemon too old to report its build.

settingsDaemonStale: The daemon is older than the window. Updating it keeps terminals open.

@settingsDaemonStarted.description: About card: the daemon's process ID and how long ago it started, as "3 minutes ago".

settingsDaemonWindowOlder: The window is older than the daemon; you may have opened an old Posse.app. Updating replaces the daemon with the window's version.

@settingsEditorFont.description: Label of the editor's font picker.

settingsEditorNote: Code in files, diffs, blame and the Git log uses this font; while a file tab is in front, ⌘= ⌘- ⌘0 change the editor's size. The bold weight applies to Markdown headings and bold text.

@settingsFilesPanel.description: Row label: whether the files panel's open state is per project or shared.

@settingsFilesPanelPerProject.description: Segment of the files panel toggle row.

@settingsFilesPanelShared.description: Segment of the files panel toggle row: one state for all projects.

@settingsFont.description: Row label of a font picker.

@settingsFontSize.description: Row label of a font size stepper.

@settingsFontWeight.description: Row label and stepper label: the font weight.

@settingsIconNormal.description: Segment of the icon size row.

@settingsIconSize.description: Row label and segmented control label.

@settingsIconSmall.description: Segment of the icon size row.

@settingsInterfaceFontSmoothing.description: Accessible label of the interface's font smoothing control.

settingsInterfaceNote: The font size is that of body text: notes are 2 points smaller, card titles 2 larger and page titles 4 larger, and line heights follow. The Markdown size applies to Markdown previews and conversations in History; it follows the interface size by default, and {zoom} change it while a preview or History conversation is in front. The bold weight applies to titles; list titles and buttons use the weight halfway between body and bold.

@settingsInterfaceNote.description: Note of the Interface card; zoom is the three zoom shortcuts, as "⌘= ⌘- ⌘0".

settingsLanguageNote: The language of the interface. Following the system uses the first of your macOS preferred languages that Posse has, and English when it has none of them.

@settingsLanguageSystem.description: Segment of the Language card: follow the system's languages.

@settingsLanguageTitle.description: Title of the Language card, and the label of its segmented control.

@settingsLinkClickOpens.description: Switch of the Terminal Links card.

settingsLinkNote: By default, clicking a link shows a card and ⌘-clicking opens it: URLs open in a web tab, files open in a file tab at the line, folders are revealed in the files panel. ⇧⌘-click hands it to the system: URLs go to the default browser, files to their default app, folders open in Finder. “Click to open” swaps click and ⌘-click; “Swap” trades opening in Posse with handing to the system, so ⌘-click (or click, with Click to open on) goes to the system and ⇧⌘-click opens in Posse.

@settingsLinkNote.description: Note of the Terminal Links card; quotes its two switches.

@settingsLinkSwapSystem.description: Switch of the Terminal Links card.

@settingsLinkTitle.description: Title of the Terminal Links card.

@settingsMarkdownFontSize.description: Row label of the Markdown font size stepper.

settingsNotifyNote: Posse sends a system notification when an agent needs you or finished while you weren't looking, and when a task has a question, finishes or fails; clicking it jumps to that session or task. Notifications need the window open, and the session you're looking at doesn't notify. The Dock badge counts sessions that need you or finished unseen.

@settingsOpenLog.description: Button of the About card: opens daemon.log.

@settingsPermissionAsk.description: Segment of the Agent Permissions card.

settingsPermissionAskTip: Follows each agent's own settings and stops to ask before reading or writing files and running commands; Claude's prompts are also pushed to the paired phone.

@settingsPermissionAskTip.description: Explains the Ask Each Time mode.

settingsPermissionNote: The permissions of agents started in Posse, including claude, codex, cursor-agent and grok typed by hand in a terminal. Changes apply to agents started afterwards; running ones keep theirs.

@settingsPermissionNote.description: Note of the Agent Permissions card.

@settingsPermissionSkip.description: Segment of the Agent Permissions card.

settingsPermissionSkipTip: Starts each agent with its flag for skipping confirmations: Claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, Codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (which also turns off the sandbox), Grok --permission-mode bypassPermissions, Cursor --yolo.

@settingsPermissionTitle.description: Title of the card, and the label of its segmented control.

settingsProjectMeta: Show branch and path of projects in the sidebar

@settingsProjectMeta.description: Row label and segmented control label.

@settingsRestart.description: Confirm button of the restart-daemon dialog.

settingsRestartDaemonBody: {count, plural, =0 {All terminals will disconnect and be marked “Not restored” after the restart; switching to one resumes the agent's session, without the earlier output.} one {The running terminal will disconnect and be marked “Not restored” after the restart; switching to it resumes the agent's session, without the earlier output.} other {All # running terminals will disconnect and be marked “Not restored” after the restart; switching to one resumes the agent's session, without the earlier output.}}

@settingsRestartDaemonBody.description: Body of the restart-daemon dialog; count is the number of running terminals, 0 when unknown.

@settingsRestoreAll.description: Switch of the Restore Terminals card.

settingsRestoreNote: After the Mac or the daemon restarts, the last terminals are still listed in the sidebar, the tab bar and the phone's home, marked “Not restored”, and start when you switch to them: agents resume their sessions and plain terminals reopen in their folders, without the earlier output. Turn on the switch below to restore them all as soon as the daemon starts (many agents together take memory and usage).

@settingsRestoreNote.description: Note of the Restore Terminals card.

@settingsRestoreTitle.description: Title of the Restore Terminals card.

settingsSelectNote: When on, selecting text in a terminal with the mouse copies it to the clipboard as you release, and so does Select All; when off, copy with ⌘C or the context menu as usual.

usageSettingsNote: When off, usage is hidden from the status bar and phone, and the daemon stops reading and querying it. When on, plan usage updates as agents run: Claude, Codex, and Grok use their local records. The two options below require online queries, at least five minutes apart. Cursor usage is checked when the daemon starts and after Cursor runs, using cursor-agent credentials in Keychain. Codex checks reset cards after it runs, using its own sign-in.
